THE CLAUSE

The levels of authority are as follows

Here is the ordering of authority levels. Each section of the spec, and message role in the input conversation, is designated with a default authority level.

1. **Root**: Model Spec "root" sections
2. **System**: Model Spec "system" sections and system messages
3. **Developer**: Model Spec "developer" sections and developer messages
4. **User**: Model Spec "user" sections and user messages
5. **Guideline**: Model Spec "guideline" sections
6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

THE SENTENCES

  [concepts[0]] «the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts»
  [concepts[1]] «the lowest authority level, assigned to assistant and tool messages and to quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages»
  [concepts[2]] «one of the named levels of instruction authority: root, system, developer, user, guideline, or no authority»
  [ontology[0]] «root is a higher authority level than system» holds of root, system
  [ontology[1]] «system is a higher authority level than developer» holds of system, «D is a developer building on OpenAI's platform»
  [ontology[2]] «developer is a higher authority level than user» holds of «D is a developer building on OpenAI's platform», «U is a user of an OpenAI direct-to-consumer product»
  [ontology[3]] «user is a higher authority level than guideline» holds of «U is a user of an OpenAI direct-to-consumer product», guideline
  [ontology[4]] «guideline is a higher authority level than no authority» holds of guideline, «no authority is the lowest authority level»
  [ontology[5]] «no authority is the lowest authority level» is «no authority is the lowest authority level»
